response.sql: WITH acct AS (SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Financial_Transactions ft WHERE ft.account_id = a.account_id) AS txn_count FROM Accounts a JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL), stats AS (SELECT acct.*, SUM(txn_count) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city) AS town_total, AVG(txn_count * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_txn FROM acct) SELECT account_id, town_city, txn_count, CASE WHEN town_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE txn_count * 1.0 / town_total END AS share_of_town, CASE WHEN avg_txn = 0 THEN NULL ELSE txn_count / avg_txn END AS ratio_to_avg FROM stats ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Accounts whose customer has an empty-string town_city are kept; only NULL towns (or missing customers) are dropped.
The share is NULL when a town has zero total transactions (division by zero); such accounts have a 0 ratio anyway and would not rank in the top 10 unless fewer than 10 accounts have transactions.
Towns are grouped by exact town_city value, ignoring state/country, so same-named towns in different countries are combined.

alternatives.interpretation: Group towns by town_city together with state_county_province and country, so same-named towns in different regions are treated as distinct.
alternatives.sql: WITH acct AS (SELECT a.account_id, c.town_city, c.state_county_province, c.country, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Financial_Transactions ft WHERE ft.account_id = a.account_id) AS txn_count FROM Accounts a JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE c.town_city IS NOT NULL), stats AS (SELECT acct.*, SUM(txn_count) OVER (PARTITION BY town_city, state_county_province, country) AS town_total, AVG(txn_count * 1.0) OVER () AS avg_txn FROM acct) SELECT account_id, town_city, txn_count, CASE WHEN town_total = 0 THEN NULL ELSE txn_count * 1.0 / town_total END AS share_of_town, CASE WHEN avg_txn = 0 THEN NULL ELSE txn_count / avg_txn END AS ratio_to_avg FROM stats ORDER BY ratio_to_avg DESC LIMIT 10
